quest.title: Three Realms Gateway Offering: The Eve
quest.description: Learning that the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri was successfully conducted, you prepare to go pay Kokomi a visit...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Hero's Wit x3, Light Realm Sigil x80, Mora x30000

talks.objective: Go to Sangonomiya Shrine and look for Kokomi

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: ...This is the correspondence from Stingray III. Your Excellency, the situation looks extremely serious.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Thank you, Ueno. Inform Swordfish I to stand by. I'll see to the wounded shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Yes, Ma'am.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Kokomi! How've you been?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, it's you. Glad to have you back on Watatsumi Island. I would have liked to have given you a grand reception, but as you can see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Not long ago, I hosted the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri. It's the most important ceremony on Watatsumi Island. I'm guessing you'll have heard about it from Tsuyuko—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? How did you know we were the ones helping out Tsuyuko this whole time?

choices.text: I'd be more surprised if she didn't know...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Ahem. Tsuyuko is one of the more conscientious shrine maidens of Sangonomiya. I knew that handing off the planning of the ceremony to her would play to her strengths.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Based on her description of the person who took the commission, it was quite obviously you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is all starting to sound pretty suspicious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's a bit late for that now, Paimon.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Anyway. I'm sure Tsuyuko will have told you that the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri is a ceremony to reverse the Holy Soil phenomenon on Watatsumi Island.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: It's a bleaching process that slowly turns the earth to "Holy Soil," leaving the land infertile and devastating agricultural production.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Granted, crops aren't our staple food on Watatsumi Island, but I can't allow external forces to drastically alter the people's diet — and we certainly shouldn't be overly reliant on imports...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't quite follow...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Imagine all you had to eat from now on was radishes, no more fish or meat. Clearer now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Opposite day. There's something Paimon can follow.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That would be terrible!

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: The issue began with the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri. I did not miss a single step during the ritual and there's no question that the Bloodbranch Coral you retrieved was infused with the Omikami's power...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: But it didn't reverse the Holy Soil phenomenon as expected. Instead, it just... paused. This has never happened before in history.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: This is ultimately a matter of Watatsumi Island's survival, so I sent as many people as I could spare to Enkanomiya to investigate the situation.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: The news from Stingray III was that "All of Enkanomiya is engulfed in a darkness that cannot be dispelled." Additionally, there have also been reports of monsters the likes of which no one has ever seen before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Strange monsters and... an all-engulfing darkness?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: That's all that Stingray III has reported. Their investigation otherwise has yielded no useful information, and the unforgiving environment has caused many casualties so far...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I have sent several rescue teams already, but so far... the situation does not look promising.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: #It brings me no pleasure to have to ask, but on behalf of all of Watatsumi Island... I beseech you. Please lend us your assistance one more time, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Heh... please don't joke around.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: But thank you for once again agreeing to put your life on the line for the sake of our island.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Now, please come with me to meet Tsuyuko.

choices.text: For the sake of everyone on Watatsumi Island, I'll do it.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: How could you not tell, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: #Your Excellency, {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: I did wonder. Hope you're both having a wonderful date so far.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Ahem... Cut the comedy, Tsuyuko. Or I may have to have you and Naki switch posts next year — in which case, you'd be in charge of Specter Eco-Management on Watatsumi Island.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: No need, no need! I'll stop. So since the two of you are here together, I assume it's about Enkanomiya?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kokomi filled us in on what's been going on.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Oooh, "Kokomi." Hehe... ahem.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Right, well, as I'm sure Her Excellency has told you, an ominous darkness has completely engulfed Enkanomiya. At the same time, strange humanoid monsters have appeared when the place should be completely deserted.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Humanoid... monsters?

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Armor that can move on its own. I know it sounds ridiculous, but we're not talking about one spooked soldier hallucinating in the darkness. All the wounded who return to Sangonomiya have described seeing the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: On top of this, even ordinary enemies seem to grow much stronger in the darkness. That's why Stingray III has sustained so many casualties.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: There's one other thing that the returning soldiers have mentioned. They say a shrine maiden who calls herself Tsumi has been helping to treat the wounded.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Tsumi? I don't recall there being any record of a shrine maiden by that name in Sangonomiya.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: That's the thing, there isn't one. But she held something called a Sentou ceremony, which managed to keep a small area in the very center of Enkanomiya brightly lit.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Thanks to her, the wounded soldiers have a safe zone where they can recuperate.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Sentou... I've seen this term in the Deep-Sea Healing Arts Compendium. But it's a ceremony that only works in Enkanomiya, so it was never brought to Watatsumi Island.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: I'd love to meet this Tsumi... But right now, helping the wounded has to be my top priority.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Your Excellency... even if you had no duties at all right now, there's still no way we'd let you go down there.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: #Enkanomiya is exceedingly dangerous right now. Only pre-eminent warriors like {NICKNAME} and Paimon should venture there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, absolutely, a hundred percent. This is a job only we can handle!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Tsuyuko, you really get Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Hehe. We've worked together plenty of times in the past, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Do you have any other information about Tsumi?

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: It was mentioned that she wears a strange mask that covers the upper half of her face.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: How interesting. What is she trying to hide? Mmm...

response.speaker: Tsuyuko
response.text: Your Excellency, in my humblest of opinions, Tsumi has shown nothing but goodwill so far. Since the situation is so critical, we don't have the resources to make other defense arrangements and cast suspicion on our allies.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Mmm, I see what you mean.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: #I have instructed Swordfish I to proceed to Enkanomiya and continue evacuating the wounded. {NICKNAME}, you can go with them.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Swordfish I will escort you to the camp at the center of Enkanomiya.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Also — please take this with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's this? Looks like... a missing piece of something.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: It's just a little trinket. When you are faced with a difficult choice, it might be able to help you.

response.speaker: Tsuyuko
response.text: Your Excellency... but... isn't that...?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Watatsumi Island doesn't need it anymore. Besides, both of the other two pieces are in Enkanomiya. If we're lucky enough, this could be our chance to reunite them.

response.speaker: Tsuyuko
response.text: Understood, Your Excellency. Okay... emergency measures to hold the Three Realms Gateway Offering now underway.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: #Mm. I apologize for the trouble. Now, {NICKNAME}, please excuse me, I need to tend to the wounded. Please see Ueno once you're ready.

talks.objective: Venture into the darkness of Enkanomiya with Ueno

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Alright. Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Here's hoping I have the chance...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The chance to do what?

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Next year, I'm going to apply for Swordfish I to be redeployed into Specter management. 'Cause if it's that or spend more time in Enkanomiya, I'll take my chance with the Specters.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Those armor monsters... closing in on you, "ker-chunk, ker-chunk"... It's the stuff nightmares are made of.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Totally understand.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Anyway. We should be safe for now. There shouldn't be any more danger from here on out.

dialogues.speaker: Yabe
dialogues.text: Hey! Whassup!

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: It's Yabe... The odd guy from Stingray III.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You seem kinda chipper compared to all the other soldiers.

dialogues.speaker: Yabe
dialogues.text: Do I? Hehehe. I've pretty much always loved horror stories and ghost stories and stuff. Ever since I was a kid. This trip to Enkanomiya is something else, though — totally mind-blowing.

dialogues.speaker: Yabe
dialogues.text: Super fun, 10/10 would come again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Totally do not understand...

dialogues.speaker: Yabe
dialogues.text: Well, I mean, it's pretty sweet to have the chance to come to Enkanomiya. I actually kinda wanted to look into the Bunkoku Puzzle while I'm here. It's the first of the four great puzzles of Enkanomiya.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Yeah, please don't do that. We're the ones that'll have to come rescue you.

dialogues.speaker: Yabe
dialogues.text: Alright, well never mind that. There's a makeshift camp at the top of those steps over there. Yeah, you should head up and catch some rest if you haven't been there yet.

dialogues.speaker: Yabe
dialogues.text: Have you been to the camp yet? Tsumi's the one that set it up. It's over there at the <color=#00E1FFFF>top of the steps.</color>

dialogues.speaker: Yabe
dialogues.text: Gotta get yourselves familiar with the base of operations before you go venturing into the darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't want to see another masked shrine maiden disappear...

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Can't say I really understand what you're talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Anyway, if you want to rid this darkness from Enkanomiya, you can come to me for guidance. Of course... if you can trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: I'm going inside to tend to the wounded and check in with the new arrivals. Please excuse me.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After she finishes speaking, Tsumi heads to an inner room...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What're we gonna do, {NICKNAME}? Paimon really wants to trust Tsumi, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How about we go ask the wounded?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like they're resting. Let's not disturb them.

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: Hello, what can I help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there. We wanted to ask you what you know about the masked shrine maiden, Tsumi.

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: I see, I see. What're you looking to know, exactly? I've tried asking if she's seeing anyone, y'know, or whether she's looking right now... but she seems pretty tight-lipped about her love life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's... not what we meant at all. We were more wondering... do you think there's anything suspicious about her?

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: "Suspicious," huh... suspicion, the unknowable, the unpredictable... unexplored territory... Mysterious? Enigmatic? Enchanting. Bewitching. Compelling, addicting. Yeah. Know what I'm saying?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Be serious.

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: I am being serious!

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: Okay, look — if I had to pick one thing about her that's suspicious, I'd say... okay, two things. Number one, her mask. It's pretty scary, I don't know why she chose it.

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: Number two, some kind of pendant fell out of her sleeve when she was bandaging me up. It looked like it was a broken-off piece of something. So maybe when you put them together, it makes a whole.

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: Huh, maybe the other half is held by Tsumi's lifelong sweetheart...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like you hit the nail on the head. So you know, maybe ease off a little, bro?

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: Greetings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello. We'd like to ask you about the masked shrine maiden, Tsumi.

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: Because of her strange mask?

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: Well, you've come to the right person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cool!

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: I was one of the first people that she rescued. Straight away, I thought there was something very weird going on... Who is this shrine maiden who knows the lost ceremonies of Enkanomiya, and why is she covering her face with a mask?

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: So I started pestering her about it. I wasn't going to let up until I got an answer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And?

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: There weren't so many people around at that time, so eventually, she let me look behind the mask. It was actually pretty normal for the most part. There's just one thing she's trying to hide.

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: Her eyes have snake-like pupils. Thin vertical lines.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Weren't you scared?

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: I probably would have been, if every Watatsumi Islander wasn't so familiar with our legends... or I should say, our history.

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: The first familiars of the Watatsumi Omikami were the Vassals of Watatsumi. Legend has it that they are a half-human, half-snake kind who helped our ancestors fight back the Bathysmal Vishaps.

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: They were said to have disappeared long ago. But then Tsumi showed up, and as soon as I saw her snake eyes, I instinctively trusted her. It's like the vassals have returned to help us in our moment of need.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: I'm no expert, by any means. But I think Tsumi can be trusted.

talks.objective: Go to the perimeter of the camp

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Specter Eco-Management... I hear Liyue has a program to get rid of rats, cockroaches, flies, and barnacles.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Specter Eco-Management must be the same kind of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So here's what we learned from the soldiers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tsumi's mask hides her snake-eyes, which the people of Watatsumi Island believe to be a distinguishing feature of Orobaxi's vassals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Based on her actions, it seems like all she wants to do is protect the people of Watatsumi Island. And from what she said, she's doing everything she can to combat the darkness spreading in Enkanomiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So she seems pretty trustworthy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then let's go talk to her about working together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it. Like, why is she covering her pupils when they're obviously an easy way to win everyone over?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess we'll just have to see what she has to say for now. But let's keep our guard up, just in case.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: So, how's it going? Have you made a decision?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep. Let's team up to tackle the darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Okay. Then, take this.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: It's called the Bokuso Box. I found it in the Dainichi Mikoshi when I was looking for a solution.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Actually, the Dainichi Mikoshi was where I found the method and tools for the Sentou Ceremony. Lucky I can read human writing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Uhh, why wouldn't you be able to? Or did you mean it's lucky that you can read the ancient Enkanomiyan script?

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, nothing. I just meant the script in the Deep-Sea Healing Arts Compendium. I don't actually know if it's ancient or modern.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm getting more confused the more you try to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Never mind all that. Let's get back to business.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: The Bokuso Box collects light. It can dispel the darkness from the Void within a small radius.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: So for example, with the power of the Bokuso Box, you can turn monsters affected by the darkness back into their original forms.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: As it happens, there are some monsters causing trouble around the camp. Go and try out the Bokuso Box on them. I will join you shortly.

talks.objective: Use the Bokuso Box to defeat the monsters

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: You're a good fighter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You bet. We were the ones who went and got the Bloodbranch Coral that one time, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: You...! So you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Nothing. If what you say is true, then I'm sure that you'll be able to conquer the three border towers quite easily.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Also, there are a few things I need to explain to you.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: According to what I have read, the fundamental purpose of the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri is to use the serpent god's life force to awaken its second familiars: the Sangacorallia.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: They are creatures that break down raw, primitive elemental energy into the milder elemental energy of the human realm. The giant coral is a symbol that the Sangacorallia have been awakened by the serpent's blood.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: The mass awakening of the Sangacorallia causes a transformation in the ecological environment of Enkanomiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Makes sense. Even if you took away the darkness and the monsters, Enkanomiya would still look pretty different now with all the new plants and ore around.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Things are even more complicated than usual this time. The darkness from the Void Realm seems to be suppressing things in the Light Realm and the Human Realm, causing them to come to a standstill.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: You may need to use the power of the Bokuso Box to dispel the darkness and allow the ecological transformation to continue.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Please try to solve the problem using the Bokuso Box.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: I'll wait for an update from you under the statue over there.

talks.objective: Use the Bokuso Box and complete the challenge

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: It seems that you have mastered the Bokuso Box. Now, let me tell you about the ultimate purpose of this operation.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: As I said, we need to proceed to the three towers on Enkanomiya's borders. They are Towers of the Void, restored to their original form by a certain Abyss adherent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Abyss adherent? Wait, do you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: He's a purveyor of incessant nonsense. Somehow, he found out about the Three Realms and the three corners, and brought those things in using Abyssal technology.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Then, he started disseminating Abyssal energy using the towers. This caused great suffering for both the Sangacorallia and the Bathysmal Vishaps.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: I don't know why he is doing this. For us, the Abyss is highly toxic, for them... intoxicating is more the word. Addictive, but still destructive.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Maybe he just likes to toy with people and stab them in the back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows exactly who you're talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: You know him? Then it seems we have a common enemy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you bet we do!

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: To get rid of the darkness, you need to climb to the very top of the Towers of the Void and activate the Light Realm Chisel, which will let in the energy of the Light Realm.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: In Enkanomiya, the Ley Lines of the Human Realm, the elemental currents of the Light Realm, and the dark currents of the Void Realm are all exceptionally strong.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Also, I only performed the Sentou Ceremony going off the steps in the book. But I believe the key to the ceremony is the statue in front of us.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: You can offer crystals of Light Realm energy to it to increase the Bokuso Box's power. Also, resting here can restore the box's energy.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Please take this hand-drawn map. I've marked out the locations of the three towers for you. You'll need to explore one step at a time, and I'd recommend you start with this tower.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Well, that's as much help as I can offer you. I'll be waiting here for the good news.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Are you ready to venture into the dark shroud of Enkanomiya?

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: You are... different from all the others. Are you human?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well {NICKNAME} is, obviously! Just not a native of Watatsumi Island, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: And you? A human hatchling?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I doubt it.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Oh, really? Because I thought that humans lose the ability to fly when they reach adulthood, just like Bathysmal Vishaps lose the ability to see in color when they reach maturity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tsumi, you seem to know a lot about vishaps.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Wait, how do you know my name?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, the wounded soldiers mentioned you.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Oh.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We came to investigate the darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Greetings, my name is Ueno, acting captain of Swordfish I. We're here to evacuate the wounded and support the Traveler's investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Swordfish I needs to rest and reorganize before commencing the evacuation. I'll see you later.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: So you're here to help resolve this, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Very well. It's taking all the energy I have to keep this light shining. I don't have the strength to try and combat the spreading darkness, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you understand what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: The Void Realm is invading. The people of Byakuyakoku believe that there are three realms: the Vishap Realm, the Human Realm, and the Void Realm.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: The darkness spreading in Enkanomiya comes from the Void Abyss. Neither vishaps nor humans can endure it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But don't Bathysmal Vishaps like the dark?

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: No. They hate the light, but only because down here in the depths, the presence of light signifies human activity.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: In fact, the Vishap Realm is the realm of pure, primordial elemental beings. It's actually referred to as the Light Realm in most books.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: The Seven Sovereigns of the Light Realm are the seven foremost elemental dragons at the pinnacle of the raw and primitive elemental forces.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's why Tsuyuko called this the "Three Realms Gateway Offering."

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: "Three Realms Gateway Offering"... Not far off the mark, actually. But technically, I think it should be called the "Triangle Gateway Offering."

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Because the source of the darkness from the void is the three towers at the corners of Enkanomiya's triangular borders.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, the three towers! The ones where we did those trials.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: You've been there before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a long story.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Oh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, Tsumi, what's up with the weird mask?

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: To hide my face. It has to do with some things that happened as I was growing up. I just don't want to scare anyone, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Does that make me untrustworthy in your eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, not at all. You've been helping the wounded all this time, everyone must be super grateful to you. It's just that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't want to be betrayed again.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Me neither. I hate betrayal too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not yet.

dialogues.speaker: Ueno
dialogues.text: Please make sure you are fully prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: So, how's it going? Have you made a decision?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Still thinking things over.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Nothing wrong with that. Even if you're just too afraid to venture out, no one can blame you.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: Please, go and fend off the monsters. Don't forget to use the power of the box.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: I'm going to observe the movement of the darkness. I'll catch up with you shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Tsumi
dialogues.text: How is it going? Any interesting results so far?

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: As long as Tsumi stays around, we shouldn't have any problems.

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: I can feel a beard coming on. Oh! Do you guys think shaving it with a weapon would work?

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: Come on, man, please! My whole life depends on this!

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: I don't know any other girls, okay? There's no one I can introduce you to.

dialogues.speaker: Enomoto
dialogues.text: No, no, not that. There's no mirror here, so could you trim my beard for me? Just use your weapon, it'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Imaizumi
dialogues.text: I've met newly planted carrots with bushier beards than you. I think you're good.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Ah, Captain of Swordfish II. Glad to have you back on Watatsumi Island. I would have liked to have given you a grand reception, but as you can see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Not long ago, I hosted the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri. It's the most important ceremony on Watatsumi Island. I'm guessing you'll have heard about it from Tsuyuko—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? How did you know we were the ones helping out Tsuyuko this whole time?

choices.text: I'd be more surprised if she didn't know...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Ahem. Tsuyuko is one of the more conscientious shrine maidens of Sangonomiya. I knew that handing off the planning of the ceremony to her would play to her strengths.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Based on her description of the person who took the commission, it was quite obviously you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is all starting to sound pretty suspicious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's a bit late for that now, Paimon.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Anyway. I'm sure Tsuyuko will have told you that the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri is a ceremony to reverse the Holy Soil phenomenon on Watatsumi Island.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: It's a bleaching process that slowly turns the earth to "Holy Soil," leaving the land infertile and devastating agricultural production.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Granted, crops aren't our staple food on Watatsumi Island, but I can't allow external forces to drastically alter the people's diet — and we certainly shouldn't be overly reliant on imports...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't quite follow...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Imagine all you had to eat from now on was radishes, no more fish or meat. Clearer now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Opposite day. There's something Paimon can follow.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That would be terrible!

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: The issue began with the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri. I did not miss a single step during the ritual and there's no question that the Bloodbranch Coral you retrieved was infused with the Omikami's power...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: But it didn't reverse the Holy Soil phenomenon as expected. Instead, it just... paused. This has never happened before in history.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: This is ultimately a matter of Watatsumi Island's survival, so I sent as many people as I could spare to Enkanomiya to investigate the situation.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: The news from Stingray III was that "All of Enkanomiya is engulfed in a darkness that cannot be dispelled." Additionally, there have also been reports of monsters the likes of which no one has ever seen before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Strange monsters and... an all-engulfing darkness?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: That's all that Stingray III has reported. Their investigation otherwise has yielded no useful information, and the unforgiving environment has caused many casualties so far...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I have sent several rescue teams already, but so far... the situation does not look promising.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: #It brings me no pleasure to have to ask, but on behalf of all of Watatsumi Island... I beseech you. Please lend us your assistance one more time, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Heh... please don't joke around.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: But thank you for once again agreeing to put your life on the line for the sake of our island.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Now, please come with me to meet Tsuyuko.

choices.text: For the sake of everyone on Watatsumi Island, I'll do it.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: How could you not tell, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Apparently, they held the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri in Sangonomiya recently. Paimon bets Kokomi was the host.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go pay her a visit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey look, a shrine maiden taking care of the wounded. That must be Tsumi, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go ask her about what's been going on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it works! Let's go back and tell Tsumi.
